title: Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage Calendar of Time Limits
content:
Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage sets the following time limits. Every figure is the same on all six deductible options, from the Cardinal Physical Damage $2,000 Deductible to the Cardinal Physical Damage $100 Deductible.

| Time limit | Figure | Clock starts at |
|---|---|---|
| Photo inspection must be completed within | 10 calendar days | The physical damage effective date |
| Late-report review: a newly reported loss reported beyond this many days is referred to a claims supervisor | 60 calendar days | The loss date |
| Unrecovered total theft settled as a total loss after | 30 calendar days | The day the theft is reported |
| Buy-back of a recovered vehicle after settlement allowed within | 30 calendar days | The notice of recovery |
| Physical damage on a newly acquired vehicle must be requested within this many days to apply from the acquisition date | 14 calendar days | The acquisition date |
| Vehicle must be expected to be off the road at least this long to be put in storage (comprehensive only) | 30 days | Expected time off the road |

## Switches tied to time limits (every option)

| Switch | Setting |
|---|---|
| A vehicle bought new from a dealer with a bill of sale is exempt from the photo inspection | Yes |
| Lowering the deductible requires a new photo inspection before it takes effect | Yes |

## Reading the calendar

- The first five limits above are counted in calendar days; the storage minimum is the time the customer expects the vehicle to be off the road.
- How each window is counted (which day is day 0, and whether the last day is in time) is part of the rule that uses the window.
- *Hypothetical:* a vehicle whose physical damage takes effect on the 1st of a month has a photo inspection window figure of 10 calendar days from that date.
